data.narrative:
Helios is a Series A climate and energy technology company that has raised $26M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparables universe of 9 firms in the Climate & Energy sector—1 public (Lonza Group, LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($26M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage transitions yields an implied valuation of $52M. Peer-median analysis was not applicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables; while 8 same-sector peers exist, none met the criteria for same-stage or adjacent-stage clustering with similar valuation tiers, requiring a minimum of 3 datapoints to avoid false precision.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $44M (low) to $60M (high), with a median point of $52M. This range reflects the uncertainty inherent in a single-method analysis and the nascent stage of the capital stack. Key uncertainties include technology maturation risk, path to commercial deployment, and capital efficiency relative to peers. The valuation should be stress-tested against Series B financing conditions and revised as additional market data emerges.
